text:
toni (devex): Folks, saw a flaky duplicate order in the onboarding sampleapp when the user token rotated mid-submit. Posting repro and asking for SDK best-practices around safe replays after auth churn.

lee (sdk): can you share the minimal repro and where you're persisting state?

toni (devex): Sure. We persist a pending object in sessionStorage so a page crash/reload can resume. We store {idempotencyKey, verb, endpoint, createdAt, body}. On reload we re-send the stored request. Code: `sessionStorage.setItem('pending', JSON.stringify(p))`.

rachel (platform): storing full body is dangerous for PII and also increases chance of duplicate side-effects. If a token refresh happens during submit the server might accept the original late response and also accept the replay.

toni (devex): Exactly. Timeline: t0 POST /orders (pending), t1 client hits auth expiry, t2 frontend does token refresh and immediately replays pending, t3 server finishes original and returns 201, t4 server processes replay and returns 201 -> duplicate order.

lee (sdk): two quick mitigations: 1) Treat 202 as "in-flight" and prefer status-check over replaying. 2) Persist only a minimal pending marker (idempotency key + resource type) and on resume call a lightweight endpoint to check outcome before re-POSTing.

toni (devex): Does SDK provide such a helper? Would be great to avoid ad-hoc checks across apps.

lee (sdk): Not yet, but we can add `sdk.idempotency.check(key)` that does a idempotency lookup (HEAD/GET) and returns {state, payload}. That would let clients avoid re-sending if the original succeeded just after refresh.

rachel (platform): Also consider including a client namespace in the idempotency key (e.g., `${clientId}:${key}`) so server dedupe windows can be scoped per-client. Otherwise replay from a different client/process could bypass server heuristics.

toni (devex): Could we also recommend backoff adjustments when token rotation is likely? Like if a refresh is in-flight pause automatic replays for a short window?

lee (sdk): Good idea. SDK suggestion: when a token refresh event happens emit a `auth:refresh` signal; the request-resumer can subscribe and defer replay until either the refresh completes and we check idempotency, or a short grace window (e.g., 2s) elapses. This prevents blind double-posts.

toni (devex): I like that. For the sampleapp I'll stop persisting body, only save {idempotencyKey, resourcePath, createdAt}. On resume: call `sdk.idempotency.check(key)` -> if completed return result, if in_progress poll `/status` until final, else re-create with new key.

lee (sdk): That workflow matches best practices. We should add a small doc snippet and a helper flow in the JS SDK. Also warn about persisting secrets/bodies.

ci-bot: CI: sampleapps/onboarding #1024 triggered tests :runner:

toni (devex): One more question: is it safe to retire an idempotency key after creating a fresh attempt? Server may keep a dedupe window; we should mark old key as "retired" so future accidental replays won't be used.

rachel (platform): Servers often consider keys immutable for a retention period. Marking as retired client-side is fine; server-side you'd need to support a "retire" signal or just ignore duplicates if a new canonical resource exists.

lee (sdk): We'll add a short helper `resumeSafely(pending)` that implements the flow: 1) check idempotency, 2) if in progress poll, 3) if missing create new attempt and optionally tag old key retired client-side. I'll open an RFC and a small PR to the JS sampleapp.

toni (devex): Great, please tag "devex-idempotency" on the PR. I'll add an e2e that simulates a token rotation race so we don't regress.

lee (sdk): Also small UX note for sampleapp: show "pending" vs "submitted" clearly so users don't click submit twice.

toni (devex): Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
